title: Open Values Governance Ledger v0.1
description: The file that holds every proposed change to the project's data and every public response to those proposals, kept at content/governance/proposals.json. People write it by hand; pipeline/build_proposals.js reads it to build the governance index, and the governance audit checks it. It runs no live votes.

format.description: Always "open-values-governance-ledger". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the ledger format this file follows. Must start with 0.1.0.

standard.description: Always "open-values-standard", the standard this format belongs to.

updated.description: The date the ledger was last changed, as YYYY-MM-DD.

purpose.description: A sentence or two saying what this ledger is for.

principles.description: The rules the ledger follows, one short sentence each, such as "a relay may move files but must not become the authority".

publication.description: How the ledger is published: storage, relays, identity, and whether voting or ratification is open.

kAnonymity.description: The rules for when attestations may count and how small a group may be reported.

proposals.description: Every proposal in the ledger, each a full open-values-proposal record. At least one.

attestations.description: Every attestation in the ledger, each a full open-values-attestation record pointing at a proposal by id.

status.description: Whether the ledger is a format seed (examples only), active (a real community process is open), or archived.

storage.description: How the records are stored, such as "single-json-file".

relay.description: The ways records may be passed around, such as a static host or email turned into a file. A relay only moves files and has no say over them.

identity.description: How people are identified in the records, such as pseudonymous or named by choice.

liveVoting.description: Always false: the ledger does not run live votes.

contactGated.description: Always true: anyone wanting to open a real process has to make contact first.

ratification.description: A sentence saying whether any proposal can currently be ratified, and what has to happen before attestations count.

privacy.description: What must never be published in the ledger, such as email addresses, phone numbers or exact addresses.

minimumGroupSize.description: The smallest number of counted attestations that may be reported as a group, so no single person can be picked out. At least 5.

countedStatuses.description: The attestation statuses that can count towards a result, such as "submitted". The governance audit rejects "template" and "draft" here.

uncountedStatuses.description: The statuses that never count, such as "template", "draft" and "archived".

countedOnlyWhen.description: The conditions that must all hold before an attestation counts, written as short expressions such as "signature.verified === true". The governance audit requires at least two.

note.description: A sentence for readers about why the current records do not count as votes.

type.description: What kind of identity this is, such as "pseudonymous" or "attributed". No account system is needed to fill it in.

id.description: A short lowercase name for this person or group, made of letters, numbers and hyphens, such as "seed-steward". The governance audit rejects email addresses and phone numbers anywhere in the record.

display.description: The name to show readers, such as "Conscious Consuming seed steward".

method.description: How the record was signed, as a short label. The seed records use "none-template", meaning nobody signed them.

verified.description: True only when the signature has been checked and holds. The governance audit requires false for every seed record, so no example can pass as a real vote.

path.description: The repository path of the file this proposal would change, such as "content/asks-offers.json".

format.description: The Open Values format of the target file, such as "open-values-asks-offers".

baseSha256.description: The SHA-256 hash of the target file as it stood when the proposal was written, in 64 lowercase hex characters. If the file changes afterwards, the hash no longer matches and the governance audit fails until the proposal is updated.

baseHash.description: The first 8 characters of baseSha256, for showing to readers. The governance audit checks that it is exactly that prefix.

op.description: The kind of change: add an item to a list, remove an item, edit a field, set a field to a new value, or attach a note without changing data.

path.description: Where in the target file the change applies, written like a JSON Pointer starting with "/", such as "/publication/privacy". The seed records use "*" to mean every item in a list.

summary.description: One or two sentences saying what the change does.

impact.description: What the change would make better if it were adopted.

risk.description: What could go wrong if the change were adopted.

format.description: Always "open-values-proposal". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the proposal format this record follows. Must start with 0.1.0.

id.description: A unique name for this proposal, in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, such as "proposal-asks-offers-reply-safety". Attestations point at it.

status.description: Where the proposal stands: template (an example), draft, submitted, withdrawn, superseded by another, or archived. The seed ledger holds only templates and drafts.

target.description: The file the proposal would change, and the hash of that file when the proposal was written.

created.description: The date the proposal was first written, as YYYY-MM-DD.

updated.description: The date the proposal was last changed, as YYYY-MM-DD.

rationale.description: Why the change is wanted, in a sentence or two.

operations.description: The changes the proposal would make to the target file, one entry per change. At least one.

signature.description: How the proposal was signed and whether that signature has been checked.

format.description: Always "open-values-attestation". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the attestation format this record follows. Must start with 0.1.0.

id.description: A unique name for this attestation, in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

status.description: Where the attestation stands: template (an example), submitted, withdrawn, or archived.

proposal.description: The id of the proposal this attestation responds to.

stance.description: The position taken on the proposal: support, concern, needs-work, oppose, or abstain.

created.description: The date the attestation was made, as YYYY-MM-DD.

publicComment.description: What the attester wants to say about the proposal, published with the record.

signature.description: How the attestation was signed and whether that signature has been checked.

counted.description: Whether this attestation counts towards a result. It may be true only when the ledger's counting conditions all hold; every seed record has false.

privacy.description: A sentence saying what private details the record leaves out, such as "Template record; contains no private contact details."
